exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs cesarean section)
causes of hemorrhage other than uterine atony
cohort: Patients with traumatic hemorrhage (n=20,207) and women with postpartum hemorrhage (n=20,060) enrolled in the CRASH-2 and WOMAN trials
finding: Several factors, including delayed hospitalization after injury or childbirth, place of birth, mode of delivery, and specific causes of hemorrhage, were associated with an increased likelihood of blood transfusion in patients with acute severe bleeding.
mod_finding: Postpartum hemorrhage patients who had a Cesarean section had an increased likelihood of transfusion compared to those who delivered vaginally.
